subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Solid and CNS Tumours: Hepatoblastoma and Medulloblastoma

steps.tx: Malignant transformation of primitive embryological hepatic parenchymal blastema represents the most frequent primary hepatic neoplasm of childhood. Arising predominantly during the first two to three years of life, **pediatric hepatoblastoma** strongly associates with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis (APC gene mutations), and extreme prematurity. Affected toddlers present with asymptomatic abdominal distension, a firm right upper quadrant mass, weight loss, and thrombocytosis.
steps.say: Hepatoblastoma is the most common primary liver cancer in toddlers, associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome and extreme prematurity. It presents as a large painless abdominal mass.

left.title: Epidemiology and Associations
points: Peak incidence under 3 years of age (median 18 months)
Strong link to extreme prematurity and low birth weight
Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (11p15 WT2 / IGF2 overgrowth)
Familial adenomatous polyposis (germline APC mutations)

right.title: Clinical Signs and Biomarkers
points: Huge, solitary, firm right upper quadrant hepatic mass
Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) elevated in >90% of cases
Extreme thrombocytosis from tumor IL-6 / thrombopoietin
Isosexual precocious puberty if beta-hCG is secreted

steps.tx: Extravagant synthesis of oncofetal proteins provides an essential diagnostic biomarker and sensitive monitor of therapeutic response. Over ninety percent of children with hepatoblastoma demonstrate massive serum elevations of **alpha-fetoprotein in hepatoblastoma**, frequently reaching hundreds of thousands of nanograms per millilitre. Conversely, the rare, highly aggressive small cell undifferentiated histological variant exhibits low or negative AFP levels, conferring a significantly worse prognosis.
steps.say: Serum alpha-fetoprotein levels are massively elevated in ninety percent of hepatoblastoma cases. Markedly low AFP levels in small cell undifferentiated tumors indicate a poor prognosis.

rows: Small regular uniform cells resembling fetal liver
Small round blue cells, loss of INI1 (SMARCB1)
Low or normal serum AFP (<100 ng/mL)
Based on liver sector involvement on CT/MRI
Guides neoadjuvant chemotherapy and liver resection

steps.tx: Malignant embryonal neuroepithelial tumor arising in the roof of the fourth ventricle represents the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor. Typically presenting in school-aged children between five and nine years, **pediatric medulloblastoma** arises within the cerebellar vermis, rapidly obstructing normal cerebrospinal fluid pathways. Children present with signs of raised intracranial pressure and progressive truncal ataxia, causing an unsteady wide-based gait.
steps.say: Medulloblastoma arises in the cerebellar vermis in the roof of the fourth ventricle. It causes morning vomiting, headache, papilledema, and progressive truncal ataxia.

vis.alt: Microscopic histology of medulloblastoma showing dense small round blue cells and neuroimaging displaying a fourth ventricle mass.
vis.caption: Densely packed small round blue cells and Homer-Wright rosettes in pediatric medulloblastoma. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Propensity for extensive leptomeningeal subarachnoid dissemination mandates complete craniospinal neuroaxis evaluation at initial diagnosis. Medulloblastoma cells shed into cerebrospinal fluid pathways to form **drop metastases along the spinal cord**, depositing along the cauda equina and spinal leptomeninges. Complete diagnostic staging requires contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging of the entire craniospinal axis alongside lumbar CSF cytology performed two weeks postoperatively.
steps.say: Medulloblastoma frequently seeds the subarachnoid space, forming drop metastases along the spinal cord. Full craniospinal MRI and CSF cytology are essential for staging.

left.title: Clinical Presentation Triad
points: Early morning headache and projectile vomiting
Papilloedema and setting sun eye sign on fundoscopy
Truncal ataxia: unable to walk heel-to-toe or sit unsupported
Head tilt and neck stiffness from tonsillar herniation

right.title: Molecular Subgroups (WHO)
points: WNT-activated (beta-catenin): excellent prognosis (>95%)
SHH-activated (Sonic hedgehog): intermediate prognosis
Group 3 (MYC amplification): aggressive, frequent drop metastases
Group 4: most common, intermediate prognosis

steps.tx: Multimodal therapeutic regimens combining maximal neurosurgical resection, craniospinal radiotherapy, and adjuvant chemotherapy achieve high cure rates in older children. To avoid devastating neurocognitive devastation, **craniospinal irradiation protocols** are strictly avoided in children under three years of age, utilizing high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue instead. Older children receive posterior fossa boost radiotherapy with craniospinal axis coverage.
steps.say: Craniospinal radiation is withheld in children under three years to prevent severe cognitive impairment. Older children receive craniospinal radiotherapy and platinum chemotherapy.

rows: 23.4 to 36 Gy to whole brain & spine + fossa boost
Standard in children >=3 years of age
Endocrine failure, intellectual decline, secondary tumors
Children <3 years to avoid radiation toxicity

steps.tx: Malignant lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the presence of pathognomonic multinucleated Reed-Sternberg giant cells affects older children and adolescents. Representing the most frequent malignant lymphoma in adolescents, **pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma** presents with painless, firm, rubbery, non-tender cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy that persists for weeks without resolving. Mediastinal adenopathy is present in sixty percent, sometimes causing dry cough and dyspnea.
steps.say: Hodgkin lymphoma is the commonest lymphoma in adolescents, presenting with painless rubbery cervical lymph nodes and mediastinal widening on chest radiograph.

vis.alt: Microscopic histological section demonstrating binucleated Reed-Sternberg giant cells with prominent owl-eye inclusion-like nucleoli.
vis.caption: Diagnostic Reed-Sternberg cell displaying bilobed mirror-image nuclei with prominent inclusion-like nucleoli. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Pathognomonic giant transformed B-cells surrounded by a non-neoplastic polyclonal reactive inflammatory background confirm histological diagnosis. Microscopic examination demonstrates **Reed-Sternberg giant cells**, featuring bilobed or multinucleated mirror-image nuclei containing huge eosinophilic inclusion-like nucleoli resembling owl eyes. Immunohistochemistry demonstrates strong positive staining for CD30 and CD15 in classical Hodgkin lymphoma, while CD45 is negative.
steps.say: Reed-Sternberg cells display classic owl-eye mirror-image nuclei. In classical Hodgkin lymphoma, the malignant cells stain strongly positive for CD30 and CD15.

rows: Collagen bands dividing lymph node into nodules
Frequent mediastinal mass; lacunar variant cells
Scattered RS cells in background of small lymphocytes
Favorable prognosis; excellent response to therapy
Abundant atypical RS cells; scarce background lymphocytes

steps.tx: Systemic constitutional symptoms indicate biologically aggressive cytokine release and dictate risk-adapted therapeutic intensity. Ann Arbor staging designates the presence of **constitutional B symptoms in lymphoma**, defined as unexplained recurrent fevers exceeding 38.0 degrees Celsius, drenching night sweats requiring clothes changes, and involuntary loss of more than ten percent of baseline body weight over six months. Treatment utilizes response-adapted chemotherapy like OEPA/COPDAC.
steps.say: Constitutional B symptoms include drenching night sweats, weight loss over ten percent, and fevers above thirty-eight degrees. They indicate advanced stage requiring intensified chemotherapy.

left.title: Ann Arbor Staging Framework
points: Stage I: single lymph node region or lymphoid structure
Stage II: >=2 node regions on same side of diaphragm
Stage III: node regions on both sides of diaphragm
Stage IV: diffuse extranodal involvement (liver, marrow)

right.title: Pediatric Chemotherapy Regimens
points: OEPA: Vincristine, etoposide, prednisone, doxorubicin
COPDAC: Cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone, dacarbazine
PET-CT adapted to eliminate radiotherapy in responders
Over 95% cure rates in early favorable disease
